SIADH is defined *only* in the context of *hypoosmolar* hyponatremia (plasma osmolality <275 mOsm/kg). Moreover, the patient’s severe neurologic symptoms (altered mental status at Na 122) demand absolute certainty before initiating sodium correction — because over-rapid correction in non-SIADH etiologies (e.g., chronic hyponatremia from endocrine disease) carries high risk of osmotic demyelination. The only evidence-based, safe, and logically prior diagnosis — grounded *exclusively* in what is known and what is missing — is **undifferentiated hyponatremia pending plasma osmolality**. This reflects clinical reality: no definitive syndrome-level diagnosis (SIADH, adrenal insufficiency, hypothyroidism, etc.) can be confirmed without the keystone test.
